interpretation: Instruction (from ep.observe()): "wipe up the 'brown spill'." The robot is capx_robosuite_panda_wipe: a 7-DoF Panda whose end effector is a fingerless wiper (gripper: null; approach axis TCP z, the box's long side along TCP x). It has one scene camera, robot0_robotview, at (1.0, 0, 0.4) looking back at the robot, and no wrist camera. The spill was a single brown S-shaped band about 4 cm wide lying flat on the white table, covering x 0.313-0.472 and y 0.019-0.238 (robot frame). Perception split it into three flat 'brown' fragments: obj1 (0.358, 0.087), obj2 (0.362, 0.21) and obj3 (0.434, 0.168), each about 3 mm thick at z of about -0.006. The table surface measured z = -0.0113 from depth. Goal state: no brown left on the table, achieved by sliding the wiper over every part of the spill while pressed flat on the table. It was not ambiguous: there was one spill and nothing else on the table.
plan: Read the robot first. The wiper's collision spheres put it at about 12 x 5 x 3 cm with the TCP at the centre of its bottom face. Keep the wiper exactly top-down with its long (12 cm) side along world y (rh.top_down yaw 90, 8.5 degrees from the start pose, so no wrist flip). Cover the spill's whole bounding box with a back-and-forth raster rather than tracing the curve: three passes along x (TCP x 0.29 to 0.495) at y = 0.06, 0.13 and 0.20, with about 5 cm overlap between swaths, sliding sideways between passes without lifting. Find the contact height first by lowering in stages; then command the passes about 2 mm below where the TCP stopped, to keep steady contact. Check progress in the camera, then lift, park the arm out of the camera's view and verify. The plan did not change. Pass 2's image already showed passes 1 and 2 had wiped their area, so pass 3 went ahead as planned.

steps.what: Read observe(), the embodiment, objects(), the camera image, the annotated ids, the collision spheres and the coloured point cloud
steps.why: Identify the robot, tool geometry, table height and the spill's extent before moving
steps.result: The wiper box is about 12 x 5 x 3 cm with the TCP on its bottom face. Table z = -0.0113. Brown points cover x 0.313-0.472, y 0.019-0.238 in an S-shaped band (mapped as ASCII from the cloud). Step 0.

steps.what: ik_batch and check_batch on 12 raster corner poses at table height (top_down yaw 90)
steps.why: Confirm reachability, joint-limit margin and arm clearance before moving
steps.result: All reachable, with 0.23-0.81 rad from the joint limits and no singularities. The only contacts were the wiper with the flat spill ids (intended) and link7's oversized spheres. The table is not in check's model, so I relied on keeping the wiper flat.

steps.what: Moved to 6 cm above the pass-1 start (0.29, 0.06), making the wiper exactly top-down
steps.why: Stage above the raster start with the wiper flat
steps.result: Done, 66 steps. Tracking error 0 mm and approach axis (0, 0, -1). Step 66.

steps.what: Lowered in stages: to table +1.5 cm, +0.4 cm, then -0.2 cm commanded
steps.why: Find where the wiper touches the table without slamming into it
steps.result: It tracked exactly down to -0.0073. Commanded -0.0133, the TCP stopped at -0.0127 (0.6 mm short), so the wiper was resting flat on the table. Step 154.

steps.what: Pass 1: slid along +x from x 0.29 to 0.495 at y 0.06, commanded z -0.0145
steps.why: Wipe the low-y third of the spill
steps.result: Done, 102 steps. The TCP stayed at about -0.0128 and flat. The arm hid most of the spill from the camera, so the result was not visible yet. Step 256.

steps.what: Slid to y 0.13 in contact, then pass 2 along -x from 0.495 to 0.29
steps.why: Wipe the middle third. The pass ends near the table's back edge, so the camera could then see the swept area
steps.result: Done, 128 steps. The image showed every bit of brown at y below about 0.18 gone. Only the high-y lobe (y 0.18-0.24) was left. This confirmed that pressing flat at this depth wipes the spill. Step 384.

steps.what: Slid to y 0.20 in contact, then pass 3 along +x from 0.29 to 0.495
steps.result: Done, 126 steps. No brown visible, but the arm hid the lobe's area. Step 510.

steps.what: Lifted straight up to z 0.06, then parked the arm at (0.35, -0.20, 0.12)
steps.why: Clear the camera's view of the whole spill area without touching the table
steps.result: Done, 76 steps. The camera image shows a fully white table. The only 'brown' pixels are the wood floor strip above the table's back edge (v 55-61). Step 586.

steps.what: Verified with reperceive(), the coloured cloud and a 3D render, then called finish_episode
steps.why: A second, independent check (there is no second camera)
steps.result: 0 objects perceived (previously 3). 0 brown points on the table. The 5857 points in the old spill box are all white (min RGB 247, 247, 241) at table height. The render shows a clean table. Finished at step 586 of 4000.

key_images.caption: Start: the brown S-shaped spill on the white table, robot0_robotview
Start: perception split the spill into obj1, obj2 and obj3
Wiper lowered flat onto the table at the pass-1 start (contact found at TCP z -0.0127)
After passes 1 and 2: everything they covered is wiped; only the high-y lobe remains
After pass 3: no brown visible, but the arm hides part of the area
Final: arm parked aside, table completely clean
Final: camera crop of the old spill area, all white
Final: 3D render of the old spill area, clean (0 perceived objects)

lessons: With a fingerless wiper, read the collision spheres in the TCP frame to get the tool's footprint and where its bottom face sits; here the TCP was on the bottom face. Find the contact height empirically by lowering in stages: in free space the TCP tracks to under 0.1 mm, so a 0.5 mm shortfall marks contact. Commanding about 2 mm below the contact height kept steady contact through sliding passes and wiped reliably. Wiped spill disappears from the RGB image (and from depth perception), so the camera is a direct progress gauge. With a single camera looking back at the robot, the arm hides the work area, so end passes where the swept area is visible, and park the arm to one side (-y here) for the final check. A full-coverage raster of the spill's bounding box, with the long side of the tool across the direction of travel and about 5 cm of overlap, is simpler and more robust than tracing a curved spill, and cost only about 360 steps of wiping.
